Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are in the middle and the players of Australia get together in a huddle before taking their places on the field as well. Dawid Malan and Jonny Bairstow will open the innings for England. Mitchell Starc will get proceedings underway with the ball here. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, runs on the board in a pressure clash is always vital and Australia have a more than defendable total on the board. It remains to be seen how the pitch plays under lights but England have only successfully chased more than 250 runs in World Cups on two occasions and given their current form, everything is stacked against them. Can Jos Buttler and his men find some inspiration in this epic rivalry and pull off the win? Or will Australia's bowlers see them over the line? Do join us in a bit to find out.

England will be content overall with their effort but would have wanted to close out the innings much quicker after they got rid of Marcus Stoinis and Cameron Green. With the ball in hand, Chris Woakes took his confidence from the India game into this game and picked up the wicket of both Australian openers. David Willey too bowled well upfront alongside Woakes and then it was the leg spin of Adil Rashid that got a couple of important wickets in that middle phase. Mark Wood bowled his heart out but his pace simply didn't turn into wickets as the ball more often than not landed in no man's land and he ended up being expensive. Woakes came back at the death and managed to close out the final over with a couple of quick wickets to finish on a high.

Australia had the momentum coming into this game and Travis Head started off aggressively but simply couldn't get his timing right and was sent back early. David Warner seemed to have started nicely but he too fell soon and then it was the pair of Steven Smith and Marnus Labuschagne who put on a steady stand to get Australia back in the game. Smith got out in the 40s and Josh Inglis followed him to the pavilion almost instantly. Marnus brought up a gritty fifty and looked set but fell for 77 and Australia had to rebuild yet again. The two replacements, Marcus Stoinis and Cameron Green had a good partnership that seemed to be taking Australia to 300 but both batters fell just when they looked to shift gears and with overs to spare and in the end, Australia were bailed out by Adam Zampa's knock of 29 runs off just 19 balls and that took them over the 280-run mark.

A very evenly contested first innings but Jos Buttler and England will be happy with their decision to bowl first on this slowish track as they have restricted Australia to 286 runs. Australia on the other hand will feel they couldn't get out of 3rd gear and would have wanted 20-30 runs more to play with here but that late blitz from Adam Zampa would have certainly galvanized them.

Joe Root in a recent interview said England are a better side than the Aussies. However, the England side hasn't walked the talk. Toss and teams in a bit.

The Australians are, as they say, peaking at the right time. After losing two in a row they're on a roll at the moment. Yes, they'll be without Mitchell Marsh and Glenn Maxwell but they still have a lot of quality in their ranks. They'll back themselves to beat a struggling England side. They though would know, despite the poor form England are in, they are not a side to be taken lightly. A win here for them will see them almost ensure their place for the knockouts. A lot to play for. This promises to be a cracker.
